ai.literal: Rumour to rise, precious life stands; it, many know not, by good fortune.
ai.translation: My precious life sustains itself because this rumour has risen. By good fortune, the many people who spread it do not know this.
ai.modern: ஊரில் நம்மைப் பற்றிப் பழிச்சொல் எழுவதால்தான் என் அரிய உயிர் நிலைத்து நிற்கிறது. நல்ல வேளையாக, இதை அந்தப் பலரும் அறிய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The speaker finds an unexpected comfort in the public rumour about their secret love. The gossip validates their bond and gives them the strength to keep living despite the pain of separation. Ironically, the townspeople spread the rumour to shame them, unaware that they are actually keeping the speaker's hopes and life alive. It is sheer good fortune that the public does not realize the life-saving effect of their gossip.

ai.literal: Flower like eyed-she's rarity not-knowing, rumour to-us gave this town.
ai.translation: Without realizing the rarity of the girl with flower-like eyes, this town has gifted me with this rumour.
ai.modern: மலர் போன்ற கண்களை உடையவளின் அருமையை அறியாமல், இந்த ஊர் அவளைப் பற்றிய வதந்தியை எனக்கு அளித்து உதவியது.
ai.explanation: The lover speaks about the public gossip surrounding his relationship. He notes that the townspeople spread rumours without understanding how precious and hard to attain his flower-eyed lover truly is. Ironically, by linking his name with hers, the town's gossip actually brings him joy and makes him feel closer to her. The word 'alar' refers to the public chatter or scandal that reveals their secret love.

ai.literal: Does it not yield, town known scandal? That without obtaining, having obtained like nature it has.
ai.translation: Does not this scandal known to the whole town bring me joy? It has the nature of making me feel as if I have attained him, even when I have not.
ai.modern: ஊர் முழுவதும் அறிந்த இந்த வதந்தி எனக்கு இன்பம் தராதா? அவரை நான் அடையாமலேயே அடைந்தது போன்ற உணர்வை அது தருகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks about the public gossip surrounding her relationship with her lover. She asks rhetorically if this scandal does not actually bring her joy. Because their love is now spoken of by everyone, she feels a sense of union with him. The gossip creates the illusion of having attained him, even when they are physically apart.

ai.literal: By gossip, it is budding, love; if that is not, having lost nature, it will say 'tav' (fade).
ai.translation: Love buds and grows because of public gossip. Without it, love would lose its nature and fade away.
ai.modern: ஊரார் பேசும் அலரால் என் காதல் வளர்கிறது; அந்த அலர் இல்லாவிட்டால், காதல் தன் இயல்பை இழந்து சுருங்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker declares that public gossip actually nourishes their love, rather than destroying it. The word 'கவ்விது' here means budding or sprouting, showing that rumors act like a stimulus that makes passion grow. The ideophone 'தவ்' represents the idea of shrinking and fading. Without the challenge of public chatter, love would lose its vibrant nature and wither away.

ai.literal: Every time intoxicated liquor drinking is desired like that indeed love becoming public every time is sweet.
ai.translation: Just as drinking liquor is desired more with every wave of intoxication, love grows sweeter every time it becomes public knowledge.
ai.modern: கள் குடித்து போதை ஏற ஏற மீண்டும் அதைக் குடிக்க விரும்புவது போல, காதல் ஊருக்குத் தெரிய வரும்போதெல்லாம் அது இனிமையாகவே இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the public discovery of a secret romance to the drinking of liquor. Just as a person who drinks liquor desires it more with every wave of intoxication, the lovers find their passion growing sweeter every time a new rumor spreads about them. The word 'களித்தொறும்' shows the escalating nature of the joy, while 'வெளிப்படுந்தோறும்' links the sweetness directly to the public exposure of their love.

ai.literal: The seeing indeed [was] one day; rumour endures like the moon [being] seized [by] a snake.
ai.translation: We met for only a single day, but the rumour of it has spread everywhere, just like the news of a snake seizing the moon.
ai.modern: நாங்கள் ஒரு நாள் மட்டுமே சந்தித்தோம். ஆனால் அந்தச் செய்தி, பாம்பு நிலவை விழுங்கிய செய்தியைப் போல ஊர் முழுவதும் பரவிவிட்டது.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses astonishment at how quickly their secret became known. They met for just one day, yet the gossip has spread far and wide. The poet uses the striking image of a lunar eclipse, traditionally described as a snake swallowing the moon, to show how universally and rapidly the rumour has caught everyone's attention.

ai.literal: townspeople's gossip as manure, mother's word as water, grows this disease.
ai.translation: With the townspeople's gossip as manure and my mother's harsh words as water, this disease of love only grows.
ai.modern: ஊராரின் பழிச்சொல் எருவாகவும், அன்னையின் கடுஞ்சொல் நீராகவும் கொண்டு இந்த காதல் நோய் மேலும் வளர்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker compares her lovesickness to a growing plant. The public gossip of the townspeople acts as the manure that feeds it. Her mother's scolding words act as the water that nourishes it. Instead of suppressing her feelings, the opposition from her family and society only makes her love grow stronger.

ai.literal: With ghee fire we will extinguish saying, it is like that, by rumour passion we will extinguish saying.
ai.translation: Thinking that passion can be extinguished by public rumour is like saying one can extinguish a fire with ghee.
ai.modern: ஊரார் பேசும் பழிச்சொல்லால் காமத்தை அணைத்துவிடலாம் என்று நினைப்பது, நெய்யை ஊற்றி நெருப்பை அணைப்போம் என்று சொல்வதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid simile to explain the effect of public gossip on secret love. Just as pouring ghee on a fire only makes it blaze higher instead of putting it out, trying to suppress passion through the uproar of public rumour only intensifies it. The word 'கௌவை' refers to the scandalous talk in the village, which, rather than shaming the lovers into separation, fuels their devotion to each other.

ai.literal: Rumour to-be-ashamed-of is-it-possible, "fear-not dispel" he-who-said, many-people to-be-ashamed when-abandoned?
ai.translation: When the one who once said "Fear not" has abandoned me to the shame of many, is it possible for me to shy away from public rumour?
ai.modern: அஞ்சாதே என்று அன்று உறுதியளித்தவர், இன்று பலரும் வெட்கப்படும்படி என்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்த நிலையில், ஊரார் தூற்றும் பழிச்சொல்லுக்கு நான் வெட்கப்பட முடியுமோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her lover's departure and the resulting public gossip. He had previously promised to protect her and told her not to fear, but has now abandoned her in a way that makes even onlookers feel ashamed. Since he has broken his vow and left her exposed, she asks how she can possibly hide from or feel ashamed of the public rumour, as the damage is already done.

ai.literal: They if-desire will-bestow lover; we desiring rumour raises this town.
ai.translation: My lover will grant his grace only if he wishes. But this town raises the very rumour that I desire.
ai.modern: காதலர் தாம் விரும்பினால் மட்டுமே எனக்கு அன்பை அளிப்பார். ஆனால் இந்த ஊர் நான் விரும்புகின்ற அலரை (பழியை) தானே எழுப்புகிறது.
ai.explanation: The heroine reflects on the public gossip surrounding her secret relationship. She notes that her lover will only show her affection when he himself chooses to do so, leaving her at his mercy. In contrast, the town is actively spreading rumours about them, which is exactly what she wants. The word "கௌவை" (uproar or rumour) highlights the public chatter, which serves her purpose by making their love known and compelling her lover to formalize their union.
